audit.summary: The second theorem asserts a nonzero, compactly supported, smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying u₀ on ℝ³ and a T* ∈ (0,1]. Its Euler solution is in an all-order L²-Sobolev class on [0,T*) with bounded energy, and closed-interval solutions in that class exist exactly for T < T*. The C¹ norms and vorticity time-integrals are finite on shorter intervals. At T* the limsup of ‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞ is ∞, ∫₀^{T*}‖curl v‖_∞ dt = ∞, and no global smooth finite-energy solution exists; the first theorem is this last clause alone. The main caveat: the paper's blow-up quantity is ‖∇u‖_{L∞}, but Lean's limsup clause uses the sum ‖u‖_∞+‖∇u‖_∞, which is literally weaker (equivalent only via an extra interpolation argument with bounded energy).

lean_claims.plain: There is a smooth, divergence-free u₀ with rapid decay of all derivatives such that no jointly smooth (u,p) on ℝ³×[0,∞) solves unforced Euler with u(0)=u₀, u(t)∈L² for all t, and uniformly bounded energy.

There exist u₀ (rapidly decaying, smooth, div-free, compactly supported, nonzero), T*∈(0,1], and (v,p) such that all of the following hold. (1) (v,p) is an H^∞ Euler solution on [0,T*) with bounded energy. (2) For every T>0, an H^∞ solution on [0,T] exists iff T<T*. (3) For every T<T*, sup_{[0,T]}(‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞)<∞ and ∫₀^T‖curl v‖_∞<∞. (4) limsup_{t↑T*}(‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞)=∞. (5) ∫₀^{T*}‖curl v‖_∞ dt=∞. (6) No global smooth finite-energy solution exists for u₀.

paper_claims.plain: There exists u₀∈C_c^∞(ℝ³;ℝ³), divergence-free, with 0<T*(u₀)<∞, whose smooth Euler solution satisfies limsup_{t↑T*}‖∇u(t)‖_{L∞}=∞ and ∫₀^{T*}‖curl u(t)‖_{L∞}dt=∞.

coverage.why: It is stronger in several respects: T*≤1, u₀≠0, explicit maximality characterization, local bounds, and a global nonexistence clause. It is literally weaker in the blow-up clause, which uses ‖u‖_∞+‖∇u‖_∞ instead of ‖∇u‖_∞.
This is the global-nonexistence consequence (Navier–Stokes-Millennium-style breakdown at ν=0), not the quantitative blow-up statement. Global nonexistence in this class is not stated in the excerpt.

result.claim: The Lean quantity velocityC1Norm can be ⊤ even though the spatial supremum of the derivative operator norm is at most 1. For the identity field on ℝ³, ‖v‖_∞ = ⊤ makes velocityC1Norm = ⊤ while sup‖∇v‖ ≤ 1. So velocityC1Norm = ⊤ does not by itself force the gradient to be unbounded. The Gagliardo–Nirenberg step with the energy bound would be needed.

result.claim: For any velocity family v and any T, the lintegral over Ico 0 T of t ↦ vorticityNorm (v · t) is the lintegral of some measurable minorant g. So the lintegral in the statement is the lower (measurable-minorant) integral. This is the only reading under which the '= ⊤' claim is meaningful, and it is the reading the '< ⊤' local bounds use. It does not itself prove measurability of the witness.
